entries.claim: Putting the algebraic fraction in the simplest form is called reducing the algebraic fraction.
entries.quote: Putting the algebraic fraction in the simplest form is called reducing the algebraic fraction.
entries.note: Yellow box states exactly: 'Putting the algebraic fraction in the simplest form is called reducing the algebraic fraction.'

entries.claim: Step 1 of reducing an algebraic fraction: factorize both the numerator and denominator perfectly.
entries.quote: Factorize both the numerator and denominator perfectly.
entries.note: Step ① in yellow box states: 'Factorize both the numerator and denominator perfectly.'

entries.claim: Step 2: identify the domain of the algebraic fraction before removing the common factors in the numerator and denominator.
entries.quote: Identify the domain of the algebraic fraction before removing the common factors
entries.note: Step ② in yellow box states: 'Identify the domain of the algebraic fraction before removing the common factors in the numerator and denominator.'

entries.claim: Step 3: remove the common factor in both the numerator and denominator to get the simplest form.
entries.quote: Remove the common factor in both the numerator and denominator to get the simplest form.
entries.note: Step ③ in yellow box states: 'Remove the common factor in both the numerator and denominator to get the simplest form.'

entries.claim: An algebraic fraction is in its simplest form if there are no common factors between its numerator and denominator.
entries.quote: It is said that the algebraic fraction is in its simplest form
entries.note: Definition section states: 'It is said that the algebraic fraction is in its simplest form if there are no common factors between its numerator and denominator.'

entries.claim: Two algebraic fractions n1 and n2 are equal (n1 = n2) if two conditions are satisfied: the domain of n1 = the domain of n2, and n1(x) = n2(x) for each x in the common domain.
entries.quote: It is said that the two algebraic fractions n1 and n2 are equal
entries.note: The definition is explicitly stated in the yellow box: both conditions (domain equality and functional equality on common domain) are listed.
